title: Potato, roasted, fresh, peel not eaten, with butter

content.title: About
content.content: Roasted potato is made from fresh tubers that are peeled and fried in butter. It features a golden crust, tender interior, and the rich aroma of butter.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Potato is one of the most widely consumed vegetables worldwide.
Frying in butter gives a richer flavor compared with most vegetable oils.
There are many cutting styles—wedges, cubes, rounds—each providing a different texture.
Roasted potatoes are often served as a side dish with meat or fish.
Proper frying creates a crisp crust that locks moisture inside.

items.title: Rich in potassium
items.content: Potatoes provide potassium, which supports normal blood pressure and muscle function.

items.title: Vitamin C source
items.content: Vitamin C contributes to immune support and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Complex carbohydrates
items.content: Complex carbs give sustained energy and help keep you feeling full.

items.title: Beta‑carotene
items.content: Yellow and orange varieties contain provitamin A, beneficial for vision.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: A modest amount of fiber aids digestion.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Butter frying increases the dish’s calories, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Saturated fat
items.content: Butter contains saturated fats, which can affect cholesterol levels if consumed in excess.

items.title: Acrylamide formation
items.content: Very high frying temperatures may produce acrylamide, a potential harmful compound.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot as a standalone dish, a side to meat or fish, or as a snack. Sprinkle with fresh herbs, spices, or a pinch of salt for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked roasted potatoes in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat in an oven or skillet to restore crispness.
